audience: Solo web developers and vibe coders
core_mechanic: Not a mechanic: a market event that rewards small original browser games with a hard deadline, which is the same shape as a one-session build
monetization: Prize competition, monetized via Nitro ads
title: Sixty-Five Thousand: a contest that pays for scope discipline, not scope
why_hot: Nitro and Base44 opened a 65,000 USD browser game contest on 2026-11-05 with submissions through 2026-12-03 and a 25,000 USD grand prize, judged on gameplay, creativity and technical execution

audience: Desktop and mobile players who want a two-minute daily ritual with a leaderboard
core_mechanic: A short physics track is seeded from the UTC day; every player races the identical geometry against a deterministic rival, and the only visible comparison is your time against your own previous best on that seed
title: Ghost Shift: one seeded track per UTC day, one rival, rank only against your own last run
why_hot: PolyTrack is the largest rising gaming search term at 1,220,000 monthly searches (2026-09), up 639 percent in three months, after adding a daily challenge on 2026-11-04 that resets at 00:00 UTC with the same track and car for everyone

audience: Game jam players, itch.io browser audience, keyboard desktop
core_mechanic: One modifier key reassigns the meaning of every other input; the player's skill is tracking which mapping is live rather than executing the mapping
title: Shift Key: the entire control scheme is one key that changes what every other key means
why_hot: GitHub Game Off 2026 runs through 2026-12-01 with the theme SHIFT and explicitly names 'a game where the Shift key is the only control' and 'controls that rotate every few seconds' as valid readings, so a large pool of browser entries is about to ship on this axis
